section.title: Reading Graphs of Quadratics
section.para: An object is thrown upward from a height of 5 feet with a velocity of 60 feet per second. Its height, \(h(t)\), in feet after \(t\) seconds is modeled by the function \(h(t)=5+60t-16t^2\).

image.alt: Graph of the quadratic function h(t)=5+60t−16t2 on a coordinate plane, origin O. Horizontal axis scale 0 to 4 by 1’s, labeled “time (seconds)”. Vertical axis scale 0 to 80 by 20’s, labeled “distance above ground (feet)”. Some of the points of this function are (0 comma 5), (1 comma 49), to a maximum near (1 point 9 comma 61 point 2 5) then decreasing through (2 comma 61), (3 comma 41) and (3.8 comma 0).

section.para:
Step 2 -Identify the maximum height by looking at the vertex or peak of the parabola.
approximately 62 feet

Step 3 -Identify when the object reaches its maximum by matching the maximum with its matching time from the \(x\)-axis.
approximately 1.75 seconds

Step 4 -When does the object hit the ground?
Look at where the object has a height of 0 feet, or the zero of the function. This happens at approximately 3.75 seconds. Notice there would be another zero on the graph of the function to the left of \(x=0\), but that does not make sense in the problem because the object was thrown from 5 feet.
section.title: Try It: Reading Graphs of Quadratics
section.para: A rock is launched into the air, and its height is represented by the graph below.

problem.para: What is the maximum height of the rock?
Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to find the maximum height:
Look at the peak, or vertex of the parabola.
The maximum height is 25 feet after 2 seconds.
